name: World Finer Foods, Inc.
old_description: Max H. Ries, a German immigrant who operated a textile firm in his native Munich, left Germany in 1939 and had intended to develop a similar company in Chicago. But when he arrived in the U.S., he believed he would be better off importing food. In 1947, he founded Reese Finer Foods, and its major brand “Reese” quickly became the leading brand of specialty foods in the U.S.
about:
World Finer Foods is headquartered in Bloomfield, New Jersey. The company traces its roots to 1947 when German immigrant Max H. Ries founded Reese Finer Foods after arriving in the United States in 1939. Originally intending to establish a textile business, Ries pivoted to food importing and built the Reese brand into a leading specialty-food label.

Today the firm manages and markets more than 60 premium food, beverage and personal-care brands encompassing over 1,000 products. It operates as a full-service distributor and brand manager, providing sales representation, trade and consumer marketing, finance processing (order management, invoicing, promotional spend, deductions and collections) and end-to-end logistics including EDI, FDA compliance, inventory control and warehousing on an Oracle ERP platform. The company serves as the exclusive U.S. customer for its brand partners, selling to more than 350 retail and distribution accounts.

Its client base includes domestic and international specialty-food producers such as Barry’s Tea, Marmite, Bonne Maman, Dr. Woods and London Pub, as well as its own heritage Reese line. Products reach conventional grocery, specialty retailers and e-commerce channels across the United States.

The business was built on the principle that a collective network of producers, importers and distributors could grow together. That relationship-driven philosophy remains central, underscored by membership in the Specialty Food Association, The Food Institute and status as the only U.S. member of the Circle of European Specialty Food Distributors (CEISA).
